# IATA Airport Code Lookup. Search IATA and ICAO airport codes by city, country, or airport name. View coordinates, elevation, and time zones for 500+ major airports worldwide. ### What is an IATA airport code? An IATA airport code is a three-letter alphanumeric code assigned by the International Air Transport Association (IATA) to identify airports worldwide. Kennedy International Airport in New York, LHR for Heathrow in London, and DXB for Dubai International. These codes are used on boarding passes, baggage tags, airline tickets, and flight booking systems to uniquely identify airports. ### What is the difference between an IATA code and an ICAO code? IATA codes are three-letter identifiers (e.g., LAX) used primarily in commercial aviation — on tickets, flight booking systems, and baggage handling. ICAO codes are four-letter identifiers (e.g., KLAX) assigned by the International Civil Aviation Organization and are used in air traffic control, flight planning, weather reports (METARs), and NOTAMs. Most airports have both; small or military airports may have only an ICAO code. ### How are IATA airport codes assigned? IATA codes are assigned by IATA upon application from the airport operator. The three letters are often derived from the airport or city name (e.g., ORD for O'Hare — originally 'Orchard Field'), but there is no strict rule — they are just unique identifiers within the IATA system. ### How are ICAO codes structured? ### Can I search by city name? Yes. This tool supports searching by city name, country, IATA code, ICAO code, or airport name. Type any part of the city or airport name and results will appear instantly. For cities with multiple airports (e.g., London, New York, Paris), all relevant airports will be shown in the results. For example, New York is served by JFK (John F. Some regions also have a combined metropolitan code — for example, NYC can refer to any New York area airport — but this tool shows individual airport codes. This tool shows the IANA time zone identifier (e.g., America/New\_York) for each airport. ### What are coordinates and how are they displayed? The IATA airport code system is one of the most widely recognized airline industry standards.
